episodes.214686: A frontal boundary advanced through northeastern NM and washed up to the east slopes of the central mountain chain during the morning of August 4th. Daily rounds of afternoon thunderstorms were able to develop along the mountain chain August 4th through 6th, with several producing large or accumulating hail over portions of northeastern and central NM. One storm produced large hail over Philmont Scout Ranch on the 4th, with another producing severe hail near Folsom on the 5th, and a third producing accumulating hail and minor flooding impacts along NM3 just north of Encino, NM on the 6th. Additionally, a landspout was observed by a driver on Interstate 25 near Wagon Mound along the leading edge of an approaching severe warned thunderstorm on August 5th. Shower and thunderstorm activity dissipated during the evening hours each day.
episodes.214771: A line of thunderstorms produced sporadic low-end gale-force wind gusts near the upper Chesapeake Bay.
episodes.214772: Widely scattered thunderstorms produced sporadic instances of wind damage.
episodes.214773: Widely scattered thunderstorms produced sporadic instances of wind damage.
episodes.214809: An additional shortwave in an overly moist and sheared atmosphere was in place during the afternoon of August 7, 2026. Strong-to-severe thunderstorms began to form across south-central Pennsylvania and continued moving eastward throughout the late afternoon hours, producing some isolated tree damage in Mifflin, Juniata and Cumberland Counties. Storms continued to show upscale growth with increasing instability across the Lower Susquehanna Valley, producing more concentrated areas of tree damage across Lancaster, York, and Schuylkill Counties. Multiple rounds of slow-moving heavy rainfall led to considerable flash flooding in Lancaster County, with multiple water rescues occurring across the county throughout the afternoon and evening hours.
episodes.214834: Thunderstorms developed during the afternoon and evening hours as an upper level low pressure system moved through the Ohio Valley.
episodes.214835: Several rounds of thunderstorms moved through the region during the day and into the evening as an upper level low pressure system moved through the Ohio Valley.
episodes.214924: A slow-moving thunderstorm developed over Jefferson County, dumping as much as 1-1.5 inches of rain over a localized area of downtown Birmingham. This led to flooding of low-lying streets, with a couple cars becoming stranded in water.
episodes.214961: Scattered thunderstorms impacted Middle Tennessee during the afternoon and evening hours of August 7, 2026. These thunderstorms produced damaging winds and heavy rain, particularly across Rutherford and Williamson counties. A few trees were reported down, and roadways were flooded and closed.
episodes.215386: Thunderstorms developed in a very unstable atmosphere. There was enough flow for storms to be moving, but some storms trained over one another, resulting in a couple instances of flash flooding. Localized rainfall amounts of two to four inches were observed.
episodes.215761: Numerous thunderstorms developed along and east of the Kansas Turnpike during the early morning hours of August 7th. A few reports of large hail were received, mainly across Sedgwick and Butler counties. The largest hail report was in Augusta and up to two inches in diameter with most of the rest of the reports closer to quarter size. Otherwise there was one wind report at Jabara Airport in east Wichita which measured a gust to 61 mph.
episodes.216032: A hot and humid air mass combined with strong northwest winds aloft, to bring a bout of severe storms to eastern Iowa August 7th. Several severe thunderstorms moved across eastern IA between 4pm and 10pm August 7th. Significant wind damage was surveyed in Buchanan and Linn counties with damage to crops, trees, power lines, farm buildings, and damage to siding on homes. The town of Prairieburg and rural portions of Buchanan county received the most extensive damage. In addition, three tornadoes were confirmed near Fairbank, Prairieburg and Rubio.
episodes.216162: On the 7th, a warm and moist air mass characterized by surface temperatures reaching 89F and high relative humidity produced conditional instability across central Indiana ahead of an approaching surface front. Boundary-layer heating and localized low-level convergence served as the primary triggering mechanisms, supporting severe convective cell development across the area during the mid-afternoon hours.  ||At 15:38 EST, a severe thunderstorm moved across western Rush County, generating an estimated convective wind gust of 60 mph. The strong downdraft produced direct infrastructure and tree damage along County Road 250 South, specifically concentrated between County Road 600 West and County Road 700 West. The high winds directly knocked down multiple trees and power lines, obstructing the road segment.
episodes.216212: An elongated area of low pressure, or surface trough, draped itself across the forecast area and produced heavy rain and flash flooding.
episodes.216214: An elongated area of low pressure, or surface trough, draped itself across the forecast area and produced heavy rain and flash flooding.
episodes.216232: Amid a very active weather pattern, daily chances of showers and thunderstorms thrived in the Central Appalachians. August 6th was a light day for storm activity, with only one instance of tree damage noted in Mingo County that afternoon. Storms on this particular day remained weak and did not pose any other threat to trees and power lines in the region.
episodes.216233: An active weather pattern remained in full force on August 7th as unseasonably hot temperatures worked in tandem with passing mid-level energy to produce afternoon showers and thunderstorms across the Ohio and Tennessee Valleys. Storms first transpired around midday in northeast Kentucky, producing numerous instances of downed trees due to damaging wind gusts. This was a quick window of active weather in northeast Kentucky, as storms quickly dashed eastward into West Virginia for the rest of the day.
episodes.216234: Primarily diurnally driven showers and thunderstorms continued to impact the area from August 7th to the 9th under the guise of a front approaching from the northwest and then stalling across Ohio and Pennsylvania. This resulted in the daily formation of afternoon showers and thunderstorms, which produced damaging winds that brought down trees and power lines across southeast Ohio. Given saturated ground from previous rounds of rain already that month, one to three inches of rain produced by heavy downpours in these storms was enough to cause flash flooding on several roads in Meigs County.
episodes.216235: The active weather pattern that began the month of August continued to roll on into the 7th and 8th across West Virginia. This was due to a frontal boundary approaching from the northwest that then stalled across Ohio and Pennsylvania. This primed the atmosphere with ample moisture and unseasonably hot temperatures to help spawn the daily formation of afternoon showers and thunderstorms across the state. Scattered convection that developed both on the 7th and 8th of August inflicted downed trees and power lines across of variety of locations in West Virginia due to the damaging winds associated with the storms. Given the saturated ground from previous rounds of rain, one to three inches of rain produced by heavy downpours in these storms was also enough to cause flash flooding on several roads in West Virginia. Activity remained strongly connected to the warm temperature spread, with the loss of daytime heating at sunset causing their demise each evening.
episodes.216434: A large cold front moved across Minnesota on August 7th. The environment ahead of this front was already supportive enough to develop pre-dawn thunderstorms across the eastern Dakotas and western MN. As the front continued eastward through the morning, multi-cellular clusters produced penny to half dollar size hail and isolated strong wind gusts. Most hail reports were observed in Stearns and Benton Counties. The largest hail stone measured near half-dollar size in St. Cloud. The strongest wind gust measuring 50 knots was observed at the Glencoe Municipal Airport in McLeod County.
episodes.216467: A cluster of storms over central South Carolina pushed northward into the Piedmont of central North Carolina during the afternoon and evening. Several storms became severe, producing numerous damaging wind reports.
episodes.216552: Scattered strong to severe thunderstorms developed across far northeastern Oklahoma during the evening of the 6th, along an outflow boundary from earlier thunderstorm activity to the east. The strongest thunderstorms produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.216553: Scattered strong to severe thunderstorms developed across northwestern Arkansas during the evening of the 6th, along an outflow boundary from earlier thunderstorm activity to the east. The strongest thunderstorms produced damaging wind gusts and large hail up to quarter size.
episodes.216555: Scattered strong to severe thunderstorms developed across eastern Oklahoma during the late afternoon and evening of the 7th. The strongest thunderstorm produced large hail up to quarter size.
episodes.216556: Scattered strong to severe thunderstorms developed across northwestern Arkansas during the evening of the 7th. The strongest thunderstorms produced large hail up to quarter size and damaging wind gusts.
episodes.216572: A cluster of showers and thunderstorms produced a few wind gusts in excess of 34 knots from Saint George Island to Apalachee Bay.  In addition, waterspouts were reported offshore of Mexico Beach and Tyndall AFB.
episodes.216822: A strong thunderstorm briefly produced large hail, up to two inches in diameter, during the early morning hours of August 7th 6 miles northeast of Wallace in Codington County. The large hail dented vehicles in the area.
episodes.217237: A disturbance moved through the region Friday as heat and humidity increased throughout the day. Warm temperatures and humid conditions supported increasing instability, while strengthening wind shear allowed for loosely organized clusters of thunderstorms to develop and spread across the region. Storms produced isolated damaging wind gusts in Chenango County.
episodes.217239: A disturbance moved through the region Friday as heat and humidity increased throughout the day. Warm temperatures and humid conditions supported increasing instability, while strengthening wind shear allowed for loosely organized clusters of thunderstorms to develop and spread across the region. Storms produced isolated damaging wind gusts. The greatest severe weather potential occurred across the  Wyoming Valley, where stronger instability and shear supported better storm organization.
episodes.217273: A cold front passing over Lake Superior on the 7th caused thunderstorms that drove wind gusts as high as 45 mph.
episodes.217363: A severe thunderstorm produced quarter size hail during the evening hours.
episodes.217367: Severe thunderstorms including supercells developed during the morning hours. These storms produced severe hail across parts of northwest MN, including hail ranging from golf ball to baseball size in the Park Rapids, MN area.
episodes.217447: A shortwave moving through a large-scale trough created rounds of showers and thunderstorms on August 7th. A cluster of stronger storms across Westmoreland and Allegheny Counties created some instances of tree and power line damage. Also,|Slow-moving thunderstorms and showers in an environment characterized by 1.8 inch  precipitable water values created isolated flooding across the region. Some areas observed 2-3 inches of rain in 6 hours.
episodes.217601: On August 7, 2026, a cold front interacting with a warm, unstable air mass triggered a broken line of severe thunderstorms across central and north-central Minnesota. As the storm complex moved eastward toward the Brainerd Lakes region, localized severe cells prompted warnings for strong straight-line wind gusts near 60 mph and large hail. Communities throughout Crow Wing and nearby Cass counties experienced isolated hail falls and gusty winds, causing minor tree damage.
episodes.217636: A thunderstorm complex, driven by strong warm air advection across southern Kansas, moved across parts of northern and central Oklahoma on the morning and afternoon of the 7th. This activity produced occasional reports of severe weather (large hail and/or damaging winds), particularly across Kingfisher County, Oklahoma.
episodes.217750: High pressure over the western Atlantic, a Bermuda high, set up a warm and humid environment ahead of broad upper level trough of low pressure that slowly pushed east. Daytime heating produced sufficient instability for showers and thunderstorms to develop, some of which produced torrential downpours. Locally heavy rainfall led to several roadways flooding.
episodes.217889: During the late night of the 6th into the early AM hours of the 7th, a complex of storms moved from north to south through the combined OK/TX Panhandles, entering the OK Panhandle first. As this complex moved through it produced thunderstorm winds damage in the OK Panhandle with winds continuing to be measured well above 60 mph by ground stations throughout the area. One isolated updraft produced hail up to the size of nickels near Boise City, OK. After the thunderstorm stopped, decaying showers continued to bring strong winds to the surface from aloft and strong winds continued to be measured by ground stations.
episodes.217890: During the late night of the 6th into the early AM hours of the 7th, a complex of storms moved from north to south through the combined OK/TX Panhandles, entering the OK Panhandle first. As this complex moved through it produced thunderstorm winds damage in the OK Panhandle with winds continuing to be measured well above 60 mph by ground stations throughout the area. One isolated updraft produced hail up to the size of nickels near Boise City, OK. After the thunderstorm stopped, decaying showers continued to bring strong winds to the surface from aloft and strong winds continued to be measured by ground stations.
episodes.217896: Scattered storms moved across central Virginia on August 7. These storms produced damaging winds.
episodes.217912: Scattered nocturnal thunderstorms developed along a frontal boundary with 2000-3000 J/kg MUCAPE and around 30 knots of effective shear. Stronger storms produced hail up to half-dollar size.
episodes.217934: A warm and moist southerly flow along the western edge of high pressure centered across the Atlantic supported waterspouts across coastal waters during morning hours.
episodes.217958: Between August 7 and 9, a weakness emerged along the eastern periphery of a prominent mid-level ridge centered over New Mexico. This atmospheric feature prompted the formation of isolated to scattered thunderstorms across North Texas. A select number of these storms produced localized wind damage and small hail.
episodes.218068: Hot and humid conditions were in place across eastern New York on August 6-7, 2026. Heat index values reached between 95 and 100 degrees across portions of the Hudson Valley on August 6 with these values continuing into August 7 for portions of the mid-Hudson Valley. In addition, scattered showers and thunderstorms developed each afternoon into the early evening resulting in some incidents of wind damage as well as localized flash flooding.
episodes.218094: Slow-moving thunderstorms and showers created isolated flooding across the region. Some areas observed 2-3 inches of rain in 6 hours.
episodes.218252: A stalled surface boundary led to the development of localized severe hail storms across southwest Kansas, with reported up to two inch in diameter.
episodes.218336: An upper high over the southwest kept northeast flow over the region. Low level moisture remained high with southeast surface winds up to the Rio Grande Valley.  Severe thunderstorms developed over the Tularosa basin and brought wind gusts up to 69 mph to the WSMR.
episodes.218340: An upper high over the southwest kept northeast flow over the region. Low level moisture remained high with southeast surface winds pushing moisture just west of the Rio Grande Valley. Slow moving thunderstorms east of Deming resulted in flash flooding along NM-143.
episodes.218341: An upper high near Las Vegas, NV brought weak north to northeast flow over the region. Drier air at the surface moved in with dew point depressions over 50 degrees. An upper level disturbance helped thunderstorms develop over the Sacramento Mountains and moved into Otero and Dona Ana counties producing severe wind gusts and dust storms.
episodes.218355: Scattered thunderstorms and storms clusters developed across the western Carolinas throughout the afternoon. One storm became severe shortly after moving into Gaston County from South Carolina and produced sporadic damaging wind gusts. A series of slow-moving storm clusters produced very heavy rainfall and localized flash flooding in Rutherford and Polk Counties.
episodes.218435: A slow-moving upper-level trough over the Mississippi Valley maintained moist, unstable air across the region. Weak steering winds allowed slow-moving afternoon thunderstorms to develop over the Cumberland Plateau and mountains, producing localized flash flooding.
episodes.218498: Thunderstorms producing downpours resulted in flash flooding across New Jersey. Multiple cars were stuck in flood waters along with multiple water rescues.
episodes.218510: Thunderstorms producing downpours resulted in flash flooding across the Lower Hudson River Valley. Multiple cars were stuck in flood waters along with multiple water rescues.
episodes.218517: Thunderstorms producing downpours resulted in flash flooding across southern Connecticut. Multiple cars were stuck in flood waters along with multiple water rescues and 1 to 2 feet of flood waters on multiple roads making them impassable.
episodes.218590: Moderately strong high pressure centered offshore the Mid Atlantic Coast produced a deep, easterly moist flow across the Florida Keys coastal waters with little if any convective inhibition.  Clusters of showers and thunderstorms of short duration produced scattered gale-force wind gusts along the Lower and Upper Florida Keys.

events.narrative: Emergency manager reported flash flooding developed across central portions of Rutherford County after 3 to 5 inches of rain, with locally higher amounts of over 6 inches fell in just a couple of hours. The most significant impact was along Grays Creek, where a bridge on Jim Dobbins Rd was destroyed. At least one home near the bridge was isolated due to a washed out driveway. The other primary impacts were in Spindale and Forest City, where significant urban/poor drainage flooding was reported. This included the parking lot of an apartment complex in Spindale, where some water entered the first floor of some apartment units.

A well documented, large spatially, HP supercell, low-level mesocyclone produced an EF2 tornado along its 5 mile path. Most of the damage was EF1 damage to structures and trees. It is likely that this tornado had numerous short-lived vortices on the ground leading to the damage observed. Towards the end of it's path. The tornado snapped a wooden H frame power pole at its base, and also pulled four other H frames from the ground. The damage to the powerpoles suggests winds at least up to 120 MPH.
